To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the design of a 42 GHz VCSEL driver in 14 nm CMOS technology is presented.
a VCSEL driver with a 2-tap FFE was designed and implemented in a 14nm SOI CMOS process, and that the circuit achieved error-free data transmission at a data rate of up to 42 Gbps.
a 42 Gb/s VCSEL driver was designed and fabricated in a 28 nm CMOS technology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and measurement of a 42 GHz VCSEL driver with a 2-tap FFE in a 14nm SOI CMOS process.
the design of an ultra-high-speed VCSEL driver with a 2-tap FFE in a 14nm SOI CMOS process technology.
the development of high-speed optical communication links based on vertical-cavity surface- emitting laser (VCSEL)-based transceivers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented work is the first VCSEL driver with an FFE in 14 nm CMOS technology.
the presented 42 Gbps 14 nm SOICMOS VCSEL driver with a 2-tap FFE is a very promising solution for future 100 GbE applications.
the design and measurement of this VCSEL driver shows that the 14 nm SOICMOS technology is a viable technology for optical interconnects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presented 14 nm VCSEL driver with a 2-tap adjustable FFE can achieve a high data rate of 2.5 times of the 20 GHz modulation bandwidth of the used VCSEL.
we have demonstrated a 42 Gb/s CMOS driver IC for VCSELs.
we have demonstrated a 42 Gb/s CMOS driver circuit for VCSELs with an adjustable 2-taper FFE, which is suitable for high speed data transmission over multimode fiber.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a 42 Gb/s VCSEL driver can be implemented in a 14nm SOI CMOS process with a reasonable power consumption.
a 2-tap equalizer with adjustable delay can provide a good compromise between performance, power efficiency, and complexity.
the design of high-speed VCSEL drivers is possible with standard CMOS technologies, and the power consumption is comparable to the one of drivers in dedicated VCSEL technologies.
